chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Abī Khadījah, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying:
A man may rise with justice or with tyranny, and it is attributed to him, while he did not actually rise with it; then that may be his son or his grandson after him, so that is indeed what was meant.

key_terms.ابْنَ ابْنِهِ: his grandson; the son of his son
key_terms.بِجَوْرٍ: with tyranny; referring to oppressive or unjust rule
key_terms.بِعَدْلٍ: with justice; referring to just rule or upright conduct
key_terms.مِنْ بَعْدِهِ: after him; in a later generation
key_terms.وَيُنْسَبُ: it is attributed; assigned or ascribed to him

ai.seo_question: Can a statement about a person in hadith be fulfilled later through his descendants?
ai.summary: The hadith states that a description attributed to a man may not be realized in him personally, but may instead come to pass in his son or grandson. It indicates that such attributed qualities or outcomes can be fulfilled through one’s descendants, especially in matters like justice or tyranny.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Ahmad Bin Aiz, from Abu Khadeeja who said,

‘The man would be rising with justice or with tyranny and it would be linked to him (that he would be doing so), and he does not happen to be rising with it, and that happens to be his son, or a son of his son from after him, so it (that) would be it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Ahmad ibn ‘A’idh from abu Khadija who has said the following.

‘Sometimes a man is considered as practicing justice or acting unjustly and such acts are ascribed to him even if he may not have committed them but such acts are found in his sons or his grandsons after him then he will be it (the one who has in reality his practiced such acts).”
